title: Though Lonely Be Thy Path, Fear Not, for He
description: Though Lonely Be Thy Path, Fear Not, for He in Tonic Solfa to SONG TWENTY-TWO, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 336, “The Strength of the Lonely”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SONG TWENTY-TWO; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Though lone-ly be thy path, fear not, for He Who marks the spar-row fall is guard-ing thee; And not a star shines o'er thy head by night, But He hath known that it will reach thy sight.

lines: Though lonely be thy path, fear not, for He
Who marks the sparrow fall is guarding thee;
And not a star shines o'er thy head by night,
But He hath known that it will reach thy sight.
And not a grief can darken or surprise,
Swell in thy heart, or dim with tears thine eyes,
But it is sent in mercy and in love,
To bid thy helplessness seek strength above.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SONG TWENTY-TWO by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
